To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MyoD protein is restricted to fast fibres during development and that MyoD regulates fibre type in fast muscles, but not slow muscles.
MyoD protein is expressed in the fastest fibregroup of fast muscles, and that MyoD regulates fibre type in both slow and fast muscles.
MyoD protein is restricted to the fastest fibres in fast skeletal muscles, and is required for normal fibre-type balance in both fast and slow muscles in the mouse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of muscle differentiation and fibre type specification.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation and maintenance of fibre types in the mammalian skeletal muscle.
the molecular mechanisms that control fibre type specification and differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MyoD protein is expressed in the nuclei of all fast fibres, but is not detectable in slow fibres, except for a few slow fibres in the slow muscle.
MyoD regulates the maintenance of fibre type in fast muscles and is required for fibre type balance in fast and slow muscles in rodents.
MyoD protein is expressed differentially during development in fast and slow muscles and is involved in maintenance of fibre type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MyoD plays a role in the regulation of the fibre type balance in fast and slow muscle.

MyoD regulates the expression of genes that are involved in the determination of fibre type, but that the regulation of these genes is muscle-specific and that the regulation of the same gene in slow and fast fibres is different.

MyoD protein is expressed at higher levels in the fastest fibers and may be involved in the maintenance and differentiation of fast IIB/Iix fibers in fast muscle, but may also be involved in the regulation of gene expression of slow fibers in slow muscle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MyoD has distinct roles in fast and slow muscles in vivo, and may be important for the maintenance of fast IIB/Iix fibres in fast skeletal muscles.
MyoD has distinct functions in the regulation of fibre type in fast and slow muscles and is involved in the determination and/or maintenance of fast IIB/Iix fibres in rodents.
MyoD has a role in regulating fibre type in both slow and fast muscle, and that MyoD expression is not restricted to fast muscles.
